meta.name: ORACLE
meta.note: Single source of truth. Rules live in ORACLE.md. Never rewrite past forecasts. Arithmetic is done by tools/core.py.

lessons.text: A single poll should move ORACLE's current-events estimate by 5 points at most. Polling averages and several high-quality polls matter more.
Betting markets are strong benchmarks. If ORACLE differs from a busy market by more than 15 points, the briefing must say exactly why.
Ceasefire and peace-deal announcements are often premature. Don't treat one as lasting until it actually holds.
A Senate poll lead under about 4 points is close to a toss-up. In Maine in 2020, Collins beat her polls by a wide margin.

Stability bands recalibrated against 20 historical eras measured with the same formula. Calm eras (1851, 1956, 1997) sit below 0.40. Tense eras that held (Watergate, 9/11, 1979, Jan 6, 1968) sit at 0.40-0.60. Severe crises that bent the system (2008, 2020, 1933, Weimar 1923, the 1991 Soviet coup) sit at 0.60-0.75. Civil wars (49 BC, 1861) sit above 0.75, with the Bastille (0.746) right at the line. Bands are now 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.75, adding Path Omega (collapse).

In an energy shock, producer prices react more than consumer prices: September gasoline was +9.1% in CPI but +20.3% in PPI, and PPI final demand jumped 1.3% (ORACLE gave a 0.5%+ rise only 48%; history-based CLIO said 35%). When CPI energy jumps 5%+, treat a 0.5%+ PPI headline as likely (65-75%), not unusual.

predictions.question: Will Democrats win a majority (218+) of House seats in the 2026 midterms?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race calls / AP projection of House control. If not yet called on the date, keep open until called.

reasoning.clio: President's party lost House seats in 18 of 20 midterms since 1946; with approval far below 50%, average losses ~37 seats, far more than the GOP's narrow majority. Mid-decade redistricting partly offsets.
reasoning.omen: Trump approval ~36% average (Pew 30%, Reuters/Ipsos 32%), generic ballot D+7-8, CPI 3.7% and PPI 6.3%, unpopular war driving gas prices. Pre-mortem: redistricting gains plus ~$276M late Musk money and a polling miss toward Republicans could still hold the House.

predictions.question: Will Democrats win control of the Senate (51+ seats, since the VP breaks ties) in the 2026 midterms?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race calls. Count independents who caucus with Democrats as Democrats. Keep open until control is called (Alaska RCV may delay).

reasoning.clio: Net +4 Senate seats through red-leaning states is historically hard; polls have missed by 4-5 pts.
reasoning.omen: Kalshi ~65% D (SportsLine, Oct 20), Polymarket ~66% early Oct; Brown +4-6 in OH (Marist, CNN), Texas near even, Trump approval 31% (Reuters/Ipsos Oct 19). Moved toward market.

predictions.question: Will Democrat Troy Jackson defeat Sen. Susan Collins (R) in Maine's 2026 Senate race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call (Maine uses ranked-choice voting; keep open until called).

reasoning.clio: Collins has won 5 Senate races and beat her 2020 polls by ~8+ pts. Strong incumbency and crossover appeal.
reasoning.omen: Jackson leads in Washington Post-Schar School polling; national environment far worse for Republicans than 2020.

predictions.question: Will Democrat James Talarico defeat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas's 2026 Senate race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call.

reasoning.clio: No Democratic statewide win in Texas since 1994.
reasoning.omen: Polls show Talarico slightly ahead (2-3 pts); Kalshi ~50-65c D, Polymarket narrowly Paxton (Oct 20+). Moved toward market.

predictions.question: Will Democrat Sherrod Brown defeat Sen. Jon Husted (R) in Ohio's 2026 Senate race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call.

reasoning.clio: Ohio has trended R; Brown is a strong incumbent-type candidate with a record of overperforming.
reasoning.omen: Marist (Oct 15-18) Brown +4 and CNN Brown +6 over Husted; fundraising edge for Brown.

predictions.question: Will Democrat Mary Peltola defeat Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) in Alaska's 2026 Senate race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call after Alaska ranked-choice tabulation.

reasoning.clio: Alaska is Republican-leaning but Peltola won statewide in 2022; ranked-choice dynamics help.
reasoning.omen: Kalshi and Polymarket had Peltola ~73% in early Oct; polls narrow; Murkowski crossing party lines for the Democratic governor candidate. Moved toward market but stays well below it (polls only narrowly D).

predictions.question: Will Trump's approval rating in the FiftyPlusOne polling average be below 37.0% on Nov 2, 2026?
predictions.resolution_source: fiftyplusone.news/polls/approval/president, value shown for Nov 2 (or nearest prior update).

reasoning.clio: Approval averages are sticky; currently 34.6%. Moving 2.4+ pts in three weeks is uncommon without a major event.
reasoning.omen: Inflation and war headlines keep pressure on approval; a rally-around-the-flag or Iran deal could lift it.

predictions.question: Will 2026 midterm turnout reach 50.0% or more of the voting-eligible population?
predictions.resolution_source: US Elections Project (election.lab.ufl.edu) 2026 general election turnout estimate.

reasoning.clio: Only one midterm since 1914 reached 50% (2018). 2022 was ~46.6%.
reasoning.omen: Very high polarization, mass protest mobilization tied to early voting, record money, competitive Senate map.

predictions.question: Will the Federal Reserve raise the federal funds target range at its October 27-28, 2026 meeting?
predictions.resolution_source: FOMC statement on federalreserve.gov.

reasoning.clio: Fed rarely hikes back-to-back at an election-eve meeting after just hiking; reference class of consecutive-meeting hikes is thin.
reasoning.omen: Consensus (CNBC/Kiplinger/Reuters, Oct 27-28) is a hold at 3.75-4.00%; decision due Wed afternoon after this run. Prior: futures ~30% hike after PPI, since faded.

predictions.question: Will September 2026 PPI final demand rise by 0.5% or more month-over-month (released Oct 15)?
predictions.resolution_source: BLS PPI news release (bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm), headline final demand seasonally adjusted m/m.

reasoning.clio: Headline PPI final demand m/m moves of 0.5%+ are uncommon in normal months; services often offset goods.
reasoning.omen: Energy shock: gasoline +9.1% in September CPI; energy index +5.2%. Producer energy prices likely jumped similarly.

predictions.resolution_note: BLS Sept PPI (released Oct 15): final demand +1.3% m/m s.a. (forecast ~0.6%), +6.3% y/y; gasoline +20.3%. Reported by Schwab, IBTimes, TradingKey, IndexBox.

predictions.question: Will the Q3 2026 GDP advance estimate show real growth of 1.0% or more (annualized)?
predictions.resolution_source: BEA GDP advance estimate (bea.gov), released Oct 29.

reasoning.clio: Outside recessions, quarterly growth is usually above 1%; Q1 2026 printed ~1.6-2.1%.
reasoning.omen: Sept retail sales +0.8% (much of it gasoline) and Axios calls it a 'rip-roaring' economy; oil shock and falling real wages still weigh on real spending.

predictions.question: Will the October 2026 jobs report show nonfarm payroll growth below +50,000?
predictions.resolution_source: BLS Employment Situation release, headline nonfarm payroll change (first print).

reasoning.clio: Payroll growth tends to persist month to month, but first prints are noisy; Sept was ~+29k.
reasoning.omen: Fed tightening, oil shock and weakening wage growth point to continued hiring slowdown.

predictions.question: Will the S&P 500 close above 7,800 on Friday, October 30, 2026?
predictions.resolution_source: Official S&P 500 closing value (e.g., WSJ, Reuters, S&P Dow Jones Indices).

reasoning.clio: Index needs about +1% in 3 sessions; base rate for that is roughly 20-25%.
reasoning.omen: S&P rose Oct 26 and +0.6% Oct 27 (CNBC, Reuters); level estimated ~7,700-7,750 (inference, exact close not found); Fed day and big-tech earnings are two-way risks.

predictions.question: Will Brent crude front-month settle above $100/barrel on Friday, October 30, 2026?
predictions.resolution_source: ICE Brent front-month settlement as reported by Reuters, EIA, or Trading Economics.

reasoning.clio: Brent has been above $100 since early October; a 12%+ fall in 3 days is rare.
reasoning.omen: Brent closed $113.88 Oct 27 (-1.7% on Iran-talks hopes; Reuters/CNBC); needs a 12% drop by Oct 30. Pre-mortem: a sudden Iran deal could drop it fast.

predictions.question: Will October 2026 CPI inflation be 3.7% or higher year-over-year?
predictions.resolution_source: BLS CPI release for October 2026 (all items, not seasonally adjusted, 12-month change). Resolve on actual release date if different.

reasoning.clio: Reference class: y/y CPI after a +1.3% PPI jump tends to hold or rise.
reasoning.omen: Brent +6% on week to $116.72; Sept CPI already 3.74%; gasoline likely higher in Oct. Pre-mortem: late-October energy pullback or base effects.

predictions.question: Will organizers of the Oct 17 "No Kings" protests report 5 million or more participants?
predictions.resolution_source: Organizer-reported total as quoted by AP, Reuters, or another major outlet by Oct 20.

reasoning.clio: Organizers claimed 5M, 7M and 8M at the prior three national days, but this one was an early-voting day of action.
reasoning.omen: Events at 2,500+ sites but local reports of smaller crowds and no national headcount from organizers two days later; inference from absence, not a count.

predictions.resolution_note: Past its Oct 20 deadline with no verifiable organizer total quoted by AP/Reuters. Only a single republished article cited an '8 million' organizer estimate, which could not be confirmed and may be conflated with the March 28 event. Voided rather than guessed.

predictions.question: Between Oct 15 and Nov 10, 2026, will the President federalize a state's National Guard or deploy active-duty troops to a US city, citing protests or unrest?
predictions.resolution_source: AP/Reuters reporting of a new federal order (not continuation of an existing deployment).

reasoning.clio: Large US protest days are overwhelmingly peaceful; federal deployments are rare and courts have constrained them.
reasoning.omen: This administration has deployed troops to cities before (LA 2025) and is escalating against opponents (Omar raid). Election-period tension.

predictions.question: Will federal funding lapse (a full or partial government shutdown begin) after the Dec 11, 2026 deadline?
predictions.resolution_source: AP/Reuters reporting that appropriations lapsed for any federal agencies on Dec 12.

reasoning.clio: Lame-duck sessions usually pass a stopgap or omnibus; Congress chose a pre-election CR to avoid a fight.
reasoning.omen: This era saw the longest shutdown ever plus two partial shutdowns; a post-election power shift could make either side prefer to wait.

predictions.question: By Nov 14, 2026, will the US and Iran publicly announce an agreement or ceasefire that covers shipping through the Strait of Hormuz?
predictions.resolution_source: Official US and/or Iranian government announcement reported by AP/Reuters. Both sides must confirm.

reasoning.clio: Ceasefires during an active tanker war are rare and often premature; deal odds low.
reasoning.omen: Iran says 7 more tankers hit Oct 22 and threatens US bases (AP/PBS); no talks started. Small cut from 0.18.

predictions.question: Between Oct 15 and Oct 21, 2026, will at least one commercial vessel be attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz / Gulf of Oman / Persian Gulf?
predictions.resolution_source: UKMTO advisories or AP/Reuters reporting of an attack (strike, missile, drone, seizure).

reasoning.clio: Once a tanker war is underway, attacks recur weekly (1980s Tanker War; ≥9 attacks in first week of Oct 2026).
reasoning.omen: Nine attacks in or near Hormuz since Mon Oct 12, two cargo ships sunk within 24 hours (CNN Oct 15); UKMTO tally 24+ for October. Pre-mortem: only a sudden deal or pause in 'dark' escorted transits would stop attacks for a full week.

predictions.resolution_note: AP/PBS (Oct 22): Iran said 7 tankers hit overnight in Hormuz; Lloyd's List counted 28 attacks in October (UKMTO had 24 by mid-month), so more attacks landed after Oct 15. Attack claims unverified individually but reporting is by AP/Reuters as the source required.

predictions.question: Will the US military conduct strikes on targets in Yemen by Oct 31, 2026?
predictions.resolution_source: CENTCOM/DoD statement or AP/Reuters reporting of US strikes in Yemen.

reasoning.clio: US struck Houthis repeatedly in 2024-25 when shipping was threatened, but forces are stretched by the Iran conflict.
reasoning.omen: Saudi-led attacks on Yemen underway; Houthis threatening the US; Red Sea shipping risk rising.

predictions.question: Will a general Russia-Ukraine ceasefire take effect by Dec 31, 2026 and hold for at least 7 consecutive days?
predictions.resolution_source: AP/Reuters reporting that a general (not local/holiday-only) ceasefire took effect by Dec 31 and held 7+ days.
predictions.market_source: Metaculus community median ceasefire date ~Nov 2027 (as reported)

reasoning.clio: Every short truce since 2022 lapsed; no durable ceasefire in 4+ years of war.
reasoning.omen: Ukraine ended its energy-strike pause and hit a Russian refinery; Zelenskyy says he feels betrayed by Trump; drone strike on a ship in Romanian waters. Pre-mortem: a sudden US-brokered deal before winter is the main way this is wrong.

predictions.question: Will the S&P 500 close on Friday, Oct 16, 2026 above its Oct 13 close of 7,805.45?
predictions.resolution_source: Official S&P 500 closing value for Oct 16.

reasoning.clio: S&P closed 7,744.06 on Oct 15 (FRED), 0.8% below the 7,805.45 bar; a one-day gain of 0.8%+ happens on roughly 1 in 5 trading days.
reasoning.omen: Chip/AI sell-off running 7 days; hot PPI keeps rate fears alive. Pre-mortem: a dovish Warsh speech or relief rally could easily add 0.8% in a day.

predictions.resolution_note: S&P 500 closed Oct 16 at 7,659.44 (-1.09%), below the 7,805.45 bar (CNBC/Reuters wraps, Oct 16).

predictions.question: Will advance estimates show two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth among Q3 2026, Q4 2026 and Q1 2027?
predictions.resolution_source: BEA advance GDP estimates for Q3 2026, Q4 2026, Q1 2027.

reasoning.clio: Technical recessions are rare outside true recessions; growth has been positive in 2026.
reasoning.omen: Classic recession recipe forming: oil shock + Fed hiking into weak hiring + falling real wages.

predictions.question: Will the Federal Reserve raise the federal funds target range at its December 8-9, 2026 meeting?
predictions.resolution_source: FOMC statement on federalreserve.gov.

reasoning.clio: Back-to-back-to-back hikes are rare when hiring is near zero; the Fed usually waits for energy spikes to fade.
reasoning.omen: PPI 6.3% y/y, core PPI 5.0%, CPI 3.7% and rising expectations; if the Fed skips October, December becomes the live meeting.

predictions.resolution_note: S&P 500 closed Oct 23, 2026 at 7,623.68 (AP 'How major US stock indexes fared'), below 7,700.
predictions.question: Will the S&P 500 close above 7,700 on Friday, October 23, 2026?
predictions.resolution_source: Official S&P 500 closing value for Oct 23.

reasoning.clio: S&P closes above a level near the spot about half the time.
reasoning.omen: S&P near 7,712 on Oct 21 (Report.az) before a further AI-led selloff on Oct 22 (AP); 7,700 now likely overhead. Close value for Oct 23 not found.

predictions.resolution_note: DOL via Reuters/Bloomberg (Oct 22): initial claims for week ended Oct 17 fell 6k to 194,000, not above 210,000.
predictions.question: Will initial jobless claims for the week ending October 17, 2026 (released Oct 22) be above 210,000?
predictions.resolution_source: DOL weekly unemployment insurance claims report, seasonally adjusted initial claims (first print).

reasoning.clio: Claims were 199k (week to Oct 10) and ~197k before; week-to-week moves of 11k+ upward are uncommon outside turning points.
reasoning.omen: Hiring has nearly stalled (+29k Sept) and the oil shock squeezes firms, but layoffs have stayed low so far.

predictions.question: Will Josh Turek (D) win Iowa's 2026 U.S. Senate race?

reasoning.clio: Iowa has voted R at the top of the ticket in recent cycles; open-seat Senate toss-up rating.
reasoning.omen: Marist (Oct 8-11) shows a 3-pt race; an R-leaning pollster has Hinson +3. Wave environment but a lean-R state.

predictions.question: Will Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) win Georgia's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Georgia Secretary of State

reasoning.clio: Georgia is a true toss-up state; open governor seat.

predictions.question: Will Amy Acton (D) win Ohio's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Ohio Secretary of State

reasoning.omen: Marist (Oct 15-18) Acton +7; CNN likely-voter polling also has her ahead.

predictions.question: Will Abdul El-Sayed (D) win Michigan's 2026 U.S. Senate race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Michigan Secretary of State

reasoning.clio: Michigan is a swing state; midterm environment against the president's party.
reasoning.omen: Polling average El-Sayed about +3 (USPollingData, Oct 3); rated Lean D. Vance and Trump attacking him sharply (Oct 27) show GOP concern; polarizing candidate.

predictions.question: Will Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D) win Alaska's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Alaska Division of Elections

reasoning.clio: Alaska is R-leaning but ranked-choice voting and a split GOP field help a single Democrat.
reasoning.omen: Rated Lean D; three Republicans split the field; Murkowski endorsed him Oct 27 (The Hill). Count takes weeks.

predictions.question: Will Gina Hinojosa (D) defeat Gov. Greg Abbott (R) in Texas's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Texas Secretary of State

reasoning.clio: No Democrat has won Texas governor since 1990; Abbott won by 11 in 2022.
reasoning.omen: Rated Lean R; Senate race is tight but Abbott runs well ahead of a generic Republican (inference).

predictions.question: Will Rob Sand (D) win Iowa's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Iowa Secretary of State

reasoning.clio: Open seat in a lean-R state, but Sand is a statewide officeholder.
reasoning.omen: CNN likely-voter polling has the Democrat leading; Marist reports Iowa split-ticket lean (Oct 19); rated Lean D.

predictions.question: Will Jocelyn Benson (D) win Michigan's 2026 governor race?
predictions.resolution_source: AP race call / Michigan Secretary of State

reasoning.clio: Swing state; party out of the White House typically does well in midterms.
reasoning.omen: Rated Lean D; national environment strongly D (Trump approval 31-39% across polls); no verified fresh state poll (inference).

eras.name: Victorian Britain at its height
eras.like: Peace, booming trade and railways, and the Great Exhibition showing off the empire's confidence. Political fights were about religion and reform, not survival.
eras.next: Decades of relative stability and growth followed; reform came gradually through Parliament.
events: Great Exhibition opens in the Crystal Palace
Steady growth from railways and trade
Parliament fights over the anti-Catholic Ecclesiastical Titles Bill
Chartist reform movement fades after 1848

eras.name: Late-1990s boom
eras.like: Low unemployment, record stock markets and a bipartisan budget deal. The headlines were a big but orderly strike and fundraising hearings.
eras.next: The boom continued to 2000. The biggest political drama was the 1998 impeachment, which the system absorbed.
events: Stock market near record highs; unemployment under 5%
Senate hearings on 1996 campaign fundraising
Teamsters strike shuts down UPS deliveries
Clinton signs bipartisan balanced-budget deal

eras.name: Postwar calm
eras.like: Near-full employment, low inflation and a popular president running on 'peace and prosperity.' The big tension was school desegregation, where the National Guard was sent to some towns.
eras.next: Eisenhower won in a landslide. The civil-rights struggle grew slowly through the late 1950s.
events: Eisenhower campaigns for re-election on peace and prosperity
Desegregation standoffs in Clinton, Tennessee and Mansfield, Texas; National Guard called in
Steel industry back to work after summer strike
Suez Canal tension after Egypt nationalizes the canal
Economy near full employment with low inflation

eras.name: Kavanaugh fight before the 2018 midterms
eras.like: A bitterly divided Supreme Court confirmation with mass protests at the Capitol, but a strong economy with the lowest unemployment since 1969.
eras.next: Democrats won the House a month later. The economy kept growing until the pandemic.
events: Kavanaugh confirmed 50-48 after assault allegations
Unemployment falls to 3.7%, lowest since 1969
Mass protests at the Capitol; hundreds arrested
Trade-war tariffs on China escalate

eras.name: Watergate: Nixon resigns
eras.like: A president forced out by scandal, with inflation above 10% and stocks in a bear market. Yet it was orderly: courts, Congress and the press all did their jobs.
eras.next: Ford took over peacefully and pardoned Nixon. Democrats won big in the midterms, and the economy fell into recession.
events: Nixon resigns ahead of certain impeachment
Ford sworn in; peaceful transfer of power
Inflation above 10%; stocks in a bear market
'Smoking gun' tape released
House committee approves articles of impeachment

eras.name: 9/11 attacks
eras.like: The deadliest attack on US soil, the airspace shut for days, and the stock market's worst week in decades. But the country pulled together and institutions held.
eras.next: War in Afghanistan within a month, a short recession, and a long era of security politics.
events: Stock market reopens and falls 7%
National unity; the president's approval surges
Congress passes use-of-force resolution almost unanimously
All US airspace shut down for days
Terrorist attacks kill nearly 3,000 people

eras.name: Debt-ceiling showdown
eras.like: Congress came within hours of a US default, the country lost its AAA credit rating, and stocks fell sharply. Unemployment was still stuck above 9%.
eras.next: No default. Years of budget brinkmanship followed, but the recovery continued slowly.
events: Stocks fall 5.6% in a day
S&P strips the US of its AAA credit rating
Unemployment stuck at 9.1%
Debt-ceiling deal reached hours before default deadline

eras.name: Iran hostage crisis and stagflation
eras.like: Inflation above 12%, the Fed hiking rates sharply, gas worries, and Iran holding Americans hostage. A widespread feeling that things were slipping out of control.
eras.next: The hostage crisis lasted 444 days. A recession hit in 1980, and Carter lost in a landslide to Reagan.
events: Carter halts Iranian oil imports; gas worries return
Mortgage rates hit records after the Fed's sharp rate hikes
Inflation runs above 12%
Ted Kennedy launches a primary challenge to the president
Militants seize the US embassy in Tehran and take hostages

eras.name: January 6 Capitol attack
eras.like: A mob stormed the Capitol to stop the count of electoral votes, during the deadliest days of the pandemic. Congress finished the count that same night.
eras.next: Biden was inaugurated peacefully two weeks later. Trump was impeached a second time and acquitted.
events: Congress certifies the election overnight
COVID deaths hit a record of about 4,000 a day
Mob storms the Capitol to stop the electoral count
Georgia runoffs flip control of the Senate
Recording of pressure call to Georgia's secretary of state released

eras.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
eras.like: Thirteen days where nuclear war felt possible. Fear was enormous, but the country rallied behind the president and institutions held firm.
eras.next: The Soviets withdrew their missiles. A hotline and a test-ban treaty followed. Kennedy's party did well in the midterms.
events: US spy plane shot down over Cuba; nuclear war feared
Soviet ships approach the naval quarantine line
Stocks fall on war fears
Kennedy announces naval quarantine of Cuba
Congress and public rally behind the president

eras.name: Britain's Winter of Discontent
eras.like: Waves of strikes: trucks stopped, garbage piled in the streets, some of the dead went unburied. Inflation was back and the government looked powerless.
eras.next: The government lost a confidence vote in March, and Thatcher won the election in May, starting a sharp change of direction.
events: Public-sector strikes: rubbish piles up, some dead go unburied
Truck drivers' strike causes shortages
Inflation back above 9%; government pay caps collapse
'Crisis? What crisis?' headline sums up the prime minister's response

eras.name: 1968: assassinations, riots and Vietnam
eras.like: Two national leaders assassinated in two months, riots in over 100 cities, a war tearing the country apart, and campus protests everywhere.
eras.next: Chaotic Democratic convention in August; Nixon won on 'law and order.' The war and the protests went on for years.
events: Robert F. Kennedy assassinated after winning the California primary
Rising inflation and Vietnam War spending strain the budget
Vietnam casualties near their peak; protests on campuses
Poor People's Campaign encamped on the National Mall
Cities still scarred by riots after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination

eras.name: 2008 financial crisis
eras.like: The biggest bank failure in US history, credit markets frozen, Congress first voting down the bailout and the market crashing, all five weeks before an election.
eras.next: The bailout passed, Obama won, and the Great Recession deepened into 2009 before a slow recovery.
events: Congress passes $700 billion bank rescue
Credit markets freeze; companies can't borrow
House rejects the bailout; stocks plunge 7%
Washington Mutual seized: largest bank failure in US history

eras.name: Pandemic and George Floyd protests
eras.like: 100,000 dead from COVID, 40 million jobless claims, and protests and riots in hundreds of cities with curfews and troops. The most turbulent stretch in decades.
eras.next: Protests faded over the summer, the economy rebounded with huge aid, and a bitterly contested election came in November.
events: Federal forces clear Lafayette Square; troop deployment threatened
Protests and riots in hundreds of cities after George Floyd's killing; curfews
Jobless claims top 40 million since March
US COVID deaths pass 100,000
Fed and Congress pour trillions into the economy

eras.name: Soviet Union: the August coup
eras.like: Hardliners tried to seize power with tanks in Moscow, crowds defended parliament, republics declared independence, and shelves were empty.
eras.next: The coup failed in three days, and the Soviet Union dissolved within four months.
events: Coup collapses after three days
Baltic republics declare independence
Hardliners attempt a coup; tanks in Moscow
Yeltsin defies the coup; crowds defend parliament
Shortages and rationing across the country

eras.name: Weimar Germany's hyperinflation
eras.like: Money became worthless (a loaf of bread cost billions), food riots broke out, regions tried to break away, and Hitler attempted a coup in Munich.
eras.next: A new currency stopped the inflation and calm returned for a few years, but the damage to trust helped the Nazis rise after 1929.
events: The mark collapses: a loaf of bread costs billions
New currency (Rentenmark) introduced
Food riots in German cities
Hitler's Beer Hall Putsch fails in Munich
Separatist revolts in the Rhineland

eras.name: Great Depression bank panic
eras.like: The banking system was collapsing, a quarter of workers were jobless, and farmers were rioting over foreclosures.
eras.next: FDR closed every bank for a week, launched the New Deal, and confidence slowly returned, though the Depression lasted years.
events: FDR inaugurated: 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself'
Banking system collapses; states declare bank holidays
Unemployment near 25%
Farm foreclosure riots in the Midwest

eras.name: French Revolution: storming of the Bastille
eras.like: A bankrupt state, bread at record prices, the king massing troops around Paris, and then crowds seizing the Bastille.
eras.next: The monarchy lost control within weeks. A decade of revolution, terror and war followed.
events: Crowd storms the Bastille
King dismisses popular finance minister Necker
Bread prices at a 70-year high; hunger in Paris
Royal troops mass around Paris
State bankruptcy looms

eras.name: Roman Republic: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
eras.like: Decades of street violence between political gangs, a Senate trying to strip a general of his army, and the general marching on Rome instead.
eras.next: Civil war. The Republic never recovered; within two decades Rome was ruled by emperors.
events: Caesar crosses the Rubicon with his army: civil war
Tribunes loyal to Caesar flee Rome
Senate orders Caesar to disband his army
Years of gang warfare in Rome's streets

eras.name: Outbreak of the US Civil War
eras.like: Seven states had left the Union, trade between North and South had collapsed, and then Confederate guns fired on Fort Sumter.
eras.next: Four more states seceded, and four years of war killed over 600,000 Americans.
events: Lincoln calls for 75,000 volunteers
Confederates fire on Fort Sumter; war begins
Banks and trade between North and South collapse
Seven states have seceded; more are about to follow
